question: A lawsuit has been brought before a Greek court against former MEP Stelios Kouloglou for damages of EUR 450 000. The lawsuit concerns the content of a letter he had sent to the President of the European Parliament in Brussels during his term of office on issues of transparency and public interest1.

The plaintiff is the former general secretary of the Greek Prime Minister’s office – a post from which he resigned when the wiretapping scandal broke out – as well as his nephew. His actions are described in detail in the report of the relevant EP committee2.

This lawsuit falls under the provisions of Directive (EU) 2024/1069 (the ‘Anti-SLAPP Directive’), as it is directed against a person actively participating in the public debate in the public interest3.

At the same time, it also targets the political activity of a Member of the European Parliament that is directly linked to the performance of his duties, and who is protected by the independence of the mandate and the freedom of opinion of MEPs4.

In view of this, can the Commission say: What measures will it take to ensure the harmonised application of the Treaties and EU law, in particular the transposition and implementation of the Anti-SLAPP Directive in the Greek legal order?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.3.2026) The Anti-SLAPP (Strategic lawsuit against public participation) Directive1 and Recommendation2 provide a solid toolbox of safeguards and measures to fight against SLAPPs in the EU and to protect persons who engage in public participation.

In accordance with Article 81 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, which is the EU legal basis allowing the EU to take measures in this area, the Directive covers SLAPPs with crossborder implications.

With a view to expand protection to other cases of SLAPP, the Commission Recommendation has called on all Member States to ensure that their applicable framework provides for the necessary safeguards also in domestic cases. The implementation of these two instruments is a priority for the Commission.

The Directive is currently being transposed by Member States with a transposition deadline on 7 May 2026, after which the Commission will verify and ensure that Member States have complied with their obligations. The Commission closely monitors and assists Member States, including Greece, in the transposition process to guarantee effective implementation.
Measures to follow-up on the implementation of the Recommendation started immediately after its adoption and the Commission is working with all Member States, including Greece, to this end3.
1 Directive (EU) 2024/1069 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 on protecting

persons who engage in public participation from manifestly unfounded claims or abusive court proceedings (‘Strategic lawsuits against public participation’). 2 C/2022/2428 final. 3 A first overview of the information received by the Commission from Member States has been issued at the end of 2024, see SWD(2024) 292 final.
